items.headline: 26 arrested over Pasighat violence; hunger strike
items.text: East Siang police said on Monday that 26 people, five of them juveniles, are arrested over the 23 October arson in Pasighat, with eight cases filed, and urged people not to share unverified information; anti-dam activists Ebo Mili and Otul Jerang reportedly began a hunger strike in custody. Six more are held for questioning.

photo.alt: A wide river with sandbanks and a long bridge, seen between forested hills, under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: The Siang river near Pasighat, where 26 people have been arrested after the 23 October violence.

items.headline: Actor's challenge to 'Leave India' notice deferred
items.text: The Bombay High Court moved to Tuesday actor Imran Khan's challenge to a notice, citing the Immigration and Foreigners Act, to leave India by 28 October after police detained him near an election-roll protest; the US citizen and OCI cardholder says he got no hearing, and the Solicitor General appeared for the Union. Police detained him on 10 October.

photo.alt: An arched gate with Devanagari lettering over a green iron gate, leading to a tree-lined path where a few people walk.
photo.caption: The entrance to August Kranti Maidan, Mumbai, near where the actor was detained on 10 October.

items.headline: Supreme Court to hear challenge to conversion law
items.text: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and Chhattisgarh on a tribal Christian group's challenge to the state's 2026 anti-conversion law, which requires a public declaration before changing faith; neither government's response has been reported. The court tagged it with challenges to similar laws in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.

photo.alt: A domed red and cream building with an Indian flag, behind trees and a black statue on a pedestal.
photo.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi.

items.headline: A year after RSF takeover, thousands may be held
items.text: A year after the RSF captured El Fasher, Human Rights Watch says thousands of civilians may still be in RSF detention and the UN rights office estimates more than 6,000 were killed in three days; the RSF did not respond to Amnesty's findings. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain.

photo.alt: Rows of low houses and walled compounds on sandy ground, seen from the air.
photo.caption: El Fasher seen from the air, years before the war.
photo.credit: Fraktion DIE LINKE. im Bundestag / Wikimedia Commons

items.place: Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, and Gaza City
items.headline: Strike on Mawasi camp kills girl, 7
items.text: At least five people were killed in Gaza on Monday, four of them, including 7-year-old Jouri al-Soufi, in a strike on a displacement camp in al-Mawasi, Nasser Hospital said; Israel's military told AFP it was looking into the reports. Medical sources count 1,559 killed since the ceasefire.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Tents of displaced Palestinians in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, after heavy rain. Monday's strike hit a similar camp in al-Mawasi.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.headline: Albania plans curbs on protests after clashes
items.text: After weekend clashes in which police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets, Prime Minister Edi Rama, blaming the opposition and 'foreign actors', announced a bill to let police limit protests near public institutions and fine protesters up to €5,000; activists warn it threatens assembly and speech. It would also criminalise online calls for violence.

photo.alt: A large lawn in a city square with an equestrian statue, a minaret, a tower block and a red flag.
photo.caption: Skanderbeg Square in central Tirana.

items.headline: Arrests at Nairobi fuel-price march
items.text: Police arrested several protesters in running battles in central Nairobi on Monday during a march against fuel prices, after petrol rose to Sh226.96 a litre; no police statement or arrest count was reported. Organisers, the Coalition of Human Rights Defenders, say they notified police on 22 October.

photo.alt: A city street lined with shops and an office tower, with parked cars, a cyclist and pedestrians.
photo.caption: Moi Avenue in central Nairobi, one of the streets where Monday's clashes took place.

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. Four villagers are held under an anti-terror law, and after arson in Pasighat during a 23 October bandh police have arrested 26 people; two activists in custody have reportedly begun a hunger strike.
focus.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
